title: Fort Lauderdale’s 645-foot tower proposal
igCaption:
Fort Lauderdale has a 645-foot skyline proposal to watch.

Sources: The Real Deal, The Business Journals, Wikipedia

#FortLauderdale #BrowardCounty #SouthFlorida #NewBuild

scenes.text: A New York developer wants to build a 645-foot tower in Fort Lauderdale.
The proposal calls for a 645-foot tower. The Business Journals described it as 56 stories. The Real Deal said a New York developer pitched it as Fort Lauderdale’s tallest tower.
scenes.caption: The proposal calls for a 645-foot tower. The Business Journals described it as 56 stories. The Real Deal said a New York developer pitched it as Fort Lauderdale’s tallest tower.

scenes.text: Las Olas River House has 42 stories and two matching towers. It held the city’s tallest-building title until The Icon on Las Olas passed it in late 2017.
scenes.caption: Las Olas River House has 42 stories and two matching towers. It held the city’s tallest-building title until The Icon on Las Olas passed it in late 2017.

scenes.text: The city grew around the New River. One early fort sat at the fork of the river in 1838. Fort Lauderdale incorporated in 1911 and became Broward’s county seat in 1915.
scenes.caption: The city grew around the New River. One early fort sat at the fork of the river in 1838. Fort Lauderdale incorporated in 1911 and became Broward’s county seat in 1915.

scenes.text: Broward County had 1,944,375 residents in the 2020 census. Fort Lauderdale had 182,760, making it Broward’s most populous city.

scenes.text: That would add a new height mark to the downtown skyline. Downtown keeps growing, and so do the people you pass without meeting, which is exactly why NEAR exists to show you who they were.
